title: Regulatory instruments registry
description: Schema for .claude/skills/regulatory-catalogs/references/instruments.json: the registry of every regulatory instrument and framework Maxwell can cite, with titles, versions, applicability and the hard numeric requirements agents must not guess. The set of instrumentIds must equal the vocab/instruments enum exactly. Human-curated, so provenance is optional

instruments.title: Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF) for SEBI Regulated Entities
instruments.structure: NIST CSF style: function (GV, ID, PR, DE, RS, RC) . category . S<n> standard, e.g. GV.SC.S5; guidelines suffixed G<n>

hardRequirements.requirement: REs shall obtain a Software Bill of Materials for all critical systems and their components
VAPT of critical systems at least twice a year for MIIs and Qualified REs
Report cyber incidents to SEBI and CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing

instruments.description: One entry per instrument in the vocab. instrumentId must be unique across entries

instrument.description: One registry entry. An entry whose status is repealed or superseded must state repealedOn and supersededBy

instrumentId.description: Vocab identifier of the instrument; the catalog file, SLA table and every regulatoryRef use this id

regulator.description: Issuing regulator or standards body. Every regulatoryRef that cites this instrument must carry the same regulator; the schema cannot tie the pair, so loaders cross-check regulatoryRef.regulator against this entry

title.description: Official full title as printed on the instrument

shortName.description: Name used in reports and summary.md, e.g. 'SEBI CSCRF', 'RBI Directions 2026'

version.description: Circular or notification number, edition or revision as published by the regulator

issuedOn.description: Date the instrument was issued or published

effectiveFrom.description: Date compliance became or becomes mandatory; may be later than issuedOn when the regulator gave a glide path

supersedes.description: Instruments this one replaces in full; findings citing a superseded instrument should be re-mapped

status.description: Legal status of the instrument; absent means in-force. An instrument whose status is repealed or superseded is never selected as applicable to a company and is never the primary (first) regulatoryRef of a finding, risk, control or initiative: cite the instruments in supersededBy instead. It may still be cited as a secondary, historical cross-reference (a catalog mapping, or a later regulatoryRef on a record first seen before repealedOn). in-abeyance means temporarily suspended by the regulator; draft means published for consultation and not yet binding, so neither is cited as binding

repealedOn.description: Date the repeal or supersession took effect, as stated in the repealing instrument or circular. Records first seen on or after this date must cite the successor as their primary regulatoryRef; the repealed instrument may appear only as a secondary, historical cross-reference

supersededBy.description: Instruments that replace this one. When status is repealed or superseded, agents select these instead, use them as the primary regulatoryRef and re-map open findings to them; the repealed instrument may be cited only as a secondary, historical cross-reference

url.description: Canonical public URL of the instrument text

applicability.description: Who the instrument binds. Workflows intersect entityTypes with company details.entityTypes to select instruments

entityTypes.description: Regulated-entity types the instrument applies to; empty means voluntary framework applicable to anyone

jurisdictions.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, or 'EU' for union-wide law; empty means global

categories.description: Regulator-defined size or criticality tiers that change obligations, as slugs shared with company details.regulatoryRegistrations[].category (e.g. 'qualified-re'); omit when the instrument does not tier

structure.description: How controls are numbered in this instrument, so agents can form valid controlIds, e.g. 'Annex I clauses 1-40' or 'Function.Category.S<n>'

hardRequirements.description: Numeric obligations stated in the instrument (deadlines, cadences, retention periods, counts). Agents copy these values in the unit the clause states and never estimate or convert them

catalogFile.description: Workspace path of the OSCAL-lite catalog for this instrument, when one has been extracted

lastReviewedAt.description: Date a human last verified this entry against the regulator's site

topic.description: What the obligation is about; the SLA table uses the same vocabulary

requirement.description: The obligation in the regulator's own words or a close paraphrase

value.description: The number the clause states, in 'unit', exactly as stated (never converted: 3 years stays years, 15 minutes stays minutes); 1 or 0 when unit is 'boolean'

unit.description: Unit of value, as the clause states it

controlId.description: Control or clause id that states the obligation, when the instrument numbers it

reCategory.description: Alias of vocab statuses reCategory, kept for existing $refs

unit.description: Unit of a stated obligation, exactly as the clause states it: minutes, hours, days, months or years for durations; per-quarter or per-year for cadences; count for plain numbers (minimum password length, number of DR drills, number of auditors); percent; boolean for yes/no obligations. Store the value as stated, never convert between units
